summary: Sends CHOP data from one TouchDesigner process to one or more Touch In CHOP clients using TouchDesigner-optimized network transport.
key_concepts: Touch Out CHOP is the server-side sender for high-speed TouchDesigner-to-TouchDesigner CHOP data consumed by Touch In CHOP.
Touch In clients connect using the Touch Out server address and network port.
Multiple Touch In clients can receive from a single Touch Out server.
Maximum queue size prevents unbounded outgoing queued data when receivers or connections are slow.
Cook Every Frame can keep a live stream updating even when downstream demand would not otherwise cook the sender.
Synced ports use a shared global pipe, so only one process on a machine can serve synced-port data.

key_params.name: protocol
key_params.note: Streaming TCP/IP, messaging UDP, or multicast UDP

key_params.name: address
key_params.note: Destination address when protocol requires one

key_params.name: cookalways
key_params.note: Cook every frame even if downstream does not request it

key_params.name: syncports
key_params.note: Synchronize port behavior with paired Touch In

common_gotchas: Touch Out is optimized for TouchDesigner-to-TouchDesigner CHOP communication; use Pipe Out CHOP for non-TD software or devices.
The Touch In client must know the server address and port before receiving data.
Multiple Touch In clients can receive data from one Touch Out server.
Max Queue Size prevents unbounded outgoing events when a connection is slow.
Cook Every Frame can be necessary for live streams but raises cook cost.
For non-TouchDesigner receivers, use Pipe Out CHOP or DAT network operators instead.
